one_line_value_proposition: A home-based cardiac rehabilitation app — patients complete Phase III and IV rehab from home with exercise prescription, and the clinical team monitors progress remotely.
overview: myHeart is a home-based cardiac rehabilitation app for adults recovering from a heart attack or heart surgery, or living with heart failure. Patients follow a personalised exercise programme, watch educational videos and record their symptoms, weight and blood pressure. The cardiac rehabilitation team reviews this through a clinician app and can message patients. It's used alongside or instead of class-based rehabilitation.

To use it, your cardiac rehabilitation team will need training and to offer it as an option in your existing pathway. Patients need a smartphone, tablet or smart TV. It is not a 24-hour monitored service. NICE conditionally recommends myHeart while more evidence is collected. The evidence comes from NHS service evaluations rather than randomised trials. It's live in several NHS trusts, including Dorset and Derby. Pricing is by licence from the supplier, and its DTAC assessment needs refreshing.
why_it_matters_locally: myHeart has the largest documented NHS deployment among HTG761-recommended platforms, with over 20,800 UK users since 2018. The Dorset County Hospital case study demonstrated 70% CR uptake, surpassing the 2028 NHS Long-Term Plan target. Built on the my mhealth platform (which also powers myCOPD), it benefits from an established NHS relationship and DTAC completion.
target_problem_statement: Low national CR uptake rates, limited capacity for home-based CR delivery, and the 2028 NHS Long-Term Plan target to increase CR uptake to 85%.

nice_guidance_refs.note: Conditionally recommended, one of four platforms with direct clinical evidence

evidence_summary: Large real-world evidence base: UH Derby & Burton evaluation (721 patients) showed significantly lower drop-out rates with myHeart vs without. COVID-19 multi-site evaluation (5 NHS services): 89.7% of users accessed CR videos, 99.7% within first 6 weeks. Dorset County Hospital: 70% CR uptake achieved, surpassing 2028 NHS target. CUOREMA Eurostars Grant (€2.5M) for international research collaboration. NICE identifies myHeart as one of four platforms with direct clinical evidence.
evidence_strength_rationale: NICE identified one small UK three-way RCT and a 434-person real-world evaluation. Evidence supports NICE evidence generation, but the RCT is small, some evidence is observational/conference-based.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: UH Derby & Burton NHS FT evaluation
clinical_evidence_detailed.setting: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHSFT
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: 721 patients across 4 groups. Drop-out rates significantly lower with myHeart: Class+App 25.6% vs Class-only 58.2%; Home+App 42.6% vs Home-only 73.5%.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Service evaluation, not a peer-reviewed RCT. No control for confounders beyond group allocation.

clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: 89.7% of users accessed CR videos; 99.7% within first 6 weeks. Demonstrated platform utility during COVID-19 disruption to face-to-face CR services.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: COVID-19 context, rapid adoption may not reflect steady-state engagement. Sample size not stated in dossier.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: Dorset County Hospital, achieving 2028 NHS targets
clinical_evidence_detailed.setting: Dorset County Hospital NHSFT (since 2017, early adopter)
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: 70% CR uptake achieved, surpassing the 2028 NHS Long-Term Plan target. Usage increased 23.7% during COVID-19.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Service evaluation. Single-site case study at an early-adopter site, results may not be generalisable to all NHS settings.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: BACPR Annual Conference 2023, psychological outcomes poster
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: Poster presentation on psychological outcomes associated with myHeart use in cardiac rehabilitation.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Conference poster, not a full peer-reviewed publication. Detailed results not available in dossier.

clinical_evidence_detailed.setting: International collaboration, Swiss and Dutch partners
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: €2.5M Eurostars grant for biofeedback, AI algorithms, and gamification in cardiac rehabilitation. International collaboration with Swiss and Dutch research partners.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Research grant, results pending. Not yet published evidence.

clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: Conditionally recommended. myHeart assessed in two studies including one RCT. NICE identifies it as one of four platforms with direct clinical evidence suggesting potential reduction in secondary CV event risk. Over 20,800 UK users since 2018/2019.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Recommendation conditional on 3-year evidence generation period.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: NICE EAG economic model, cardiac rehabilitation platforms
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: EAG model found digital cardiac rehabilitation platforms (including myHeart) cost-saving compared with conventional rehabilitation. 275,000+ rehabilitation/education sessions delivered in 2020 across the mymhealth platform.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Generic model across all HTG761 platforms. Session count is platform-wide (includes myCOPD and other products), not myHeart-specific.
clinical_evidence_detailed.data_quality_note: 275,000+ sessions figure is across the full mymhealth platform, not myHeart-specific. Do not cite as myHeart-only activity.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: Leeds Community Healthcare NHS Trust, COVID-19 adoption
clinical_evidence_detailed.key_results: myHeart adopted during COVID-19 as a digital CR option. Part of multi-site COVID-19 adoption across NHS CR services.
clinical_evidence_detailed.study_limitation: Case study level, detailed outcome data for Leeds specifically not provided in dossier.
